key_parameters.value: 5e5 gas SPH particles; sink radius 0.5 au

evidence.quote: The two disks are modeled with $5 \times 10^{5}$ gas SPH particles
The sink radius is set to 0.5 au for all sink particles.
Both disks initially follow a power-law surface density profile of $\Sigma \propto R^{-1}$, and we adopt a Shakura–Sunyaev disk viscosity parameter of $\alpha_{\mathrm{ss}} = 0.005$.

key_parameters.value: pericenter 1500 au; initial separation 10 r_peri (3 r_peri in Run 2); node PA 15 deg, inclination 90 deg

evidence.quote: The pericenter distance is set to $r_{\mathrm{peri}} = 1500$ au, and the initial separation between the two stars is 10 times the pericenter distance.

claims.hypothesis: IRS3A and IRS3B have recently interacted through a flyby
claims.experiment: ALMA Band 7 870 um continuum imaging of the compact-array data
claims.result: A bridge about 6 arcsec (1800 AU) long and 0.8 arcsec wide links the two systems, alongside known spiral arms
claims.finding: The bridge and spirals indicate a recent prograde flyby

evidence.quote: Therefore, it is likely that L1448 IRS3A and L1448 IRS3B experienced a recent close encounter.

claims.hypothesis: Molecular lines show kinematic signatures of the interaction
claims.experiment: Moment 0 and 1 maps of H13CO+ 4-3, C17O 3-2 and H13CN/SO2
claims.result: Main bridge blueshifted and a fainter minor bridge redshifted, with H13CN/SO2 concentrated at IRS3A
claims.finding: Gas flows from IRS3B toward IRS3A, and IRS3A is in the foreground; SO2 origin would imply energetic perturbation

evidence.quote: The main bridge is blueshifted with respect to L1448 IRS3B, whereas the minor bridge is redshifted, indicating that the two structures extend in opposite directions.
If the H$^{13}$CN/SO$_{2}$ emission mainly originates from SO$_{2}$, it indicates that the L1448 IRS3A system is undergoing strong energetic perturbations.

claims.hypothesis: A prograde flyby reproduces the observed morphology and gives its timing
claims.experiment: PHANTOM SPH Run 1 with MCFOST synthetic 870 um image and CO moment 1 map
claims.result: Bridge, IRS3B spiral arm and IRS3A large-scale spiral reproduced; minor bridge and eastward arm not reproduced
claims.finding: Closest approach occurred about 15,000 yr ago

evidence.quote: The redshifted bridge connected to the eastern side of L1448 IRS3A (referred to as the minor bridge) is not reproduced in the simulation.
The hydrodynamical models suggest that the closest approach occurred about 15,000 yr ago.

claims.hypothesis: An embedded source in the IRS3B disk affects the flyby outcome and explains the IRS3B substructure
claims.experiment: Run 2 with a 50 MJ source at 300 au and accretion rate calculation
claims.result: Distinctive spiral substructures resembling observations; embedded source keeps the highest accretion rate
claims.finding: A flyby involving an embedded source can explain the IRS3B spirals and the bright compact structure around IRS3B-c

evidence.quote: The simulation shows that a close encounter involving an embedded source can produce the distinctive spiral substructures observed in the IRS3B disk
the IRS3B-c component maintains a high accretion rate throughout the simulation

referee_caveats_inferred: Orbit and disk parameters were chosen by hand with no parameter search or uncertainty, so the 15,000 yr timing has no error bar
H13CN/SO2 blend means the shock interpretation of the IRS3A emission is conditional
Run 2 uses a different initial separation than Run 1, so the runs are not directly comparable
Observational structures (minor bridge, eastward arm) are not reproduced, so the single-flyby model is incomplete
Bridge length and width are quoted without a stated measurement method or uncertainty

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Roughly tens of GB for the C40-3 execution blocks of the Band 7 project; simulations add a few GB of PHANTOM dumps
reproducibility.score_reason: Project code and key imaging settings (CASA 4.7.0, robust 0.5, self-cal intervals) and full simulation setup are given, but cell size, masks, channels, moment thresholds and MCFOST geometry are missing, and results are mostly qualitative with few numbers.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The ALMA project code is given and the simulation recipe is largely listed, but the main results are morphological and qualitative rather than numeric, and several imaging and radiative transfer settings are unstated.
